newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-Tosco lauded as it joins refiner big league.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Tosco lauded as it joins refiner big league.

text.p: Tosco Corp won plaudits from Wall Street and joined the ranks of the 'big league' in U.S. refining Monday with its purchase of Unocal Corp's 76 Products Co.

Tosco agreed to buy for $1.4 billion the fixed assets of 76 Products, including three refineries in California and 1,350 retail sites in the West Coast and Hawaii. With other considerations, the companies said the deal could be worth about $2 billion to Unocal, though the company said it would book a $375 million loss on the transaction.

According to Salomon Brothers analyst Paul Ting, the additional California plants give the acquisitive Connecticut-based Tosco a throughput of just under a million barrels of crude oil a day, or about the same in the U.S. as Amoco Corp, Exxon Corp and Mobil Corp, the nation's largest refiners.
Tosco's shares soared from Friday's close of $60-1/8 to stand at $70-1/2 by midday Monday, as the deal won braod approval on Wall Street.

"Tosco is still buying assets at the bottom of the asset cycle," said Ting. "I don't think they picked (76 Products) up for a song, as with some other Tosco purchases, but they got premium assets...and it is very accretive for shareholders," he added.

Tosco chairman and chief executive Thomas O'Malley said the deal secures the company's position as the Number One independent refiner and marketer in the country with retail fuel sales of 12 million gallons.

O'Malley also indicated that the combination of the two companies will result in significant synergies for the main refining and retailing businesses, as well as generating substantial selling, general, and administrative cost savings.
The companies and analysts said that they do not expect regulators to hold up the deal on antitrust grounds.

"From Tosco's point of view we see some very interesting upside possibilities. The amount of positive contribution will not be measured in nickles and dimes per share. But at this point the big unknown is the cost synergism," said Ting.

After the deal is completed, Tosco will have a total of four refineries in California and one in Washington, with its other two in New Jersey and Pennsylvania. O'Malley said Monday that the 76 Products plants complement each other, though some analysts said closure of one of more of the California sites is possible, and a big reduction of headcount likely in any case.
Tosco is expected to say more about its plans for the plants in briefings on Tuesday, analysts said.
Unocal, which said just three weeks ago that it was considering selling the 76 Products unit, was also seen benefitting out of the deal.
"They got a good value out of this," said Anit Sen, who follows Unocal for Wall Street brokerage Oppenheimer & Co.

The deal will reduce debt-to-capital from around 49 pct to between 40 and 44 pct and achieve a debt rating of Single-A for the company. It will allow Unocal to save $200 million to $250 million in capital expenditures on California downstream which it will redirect to the international exploration and production side, Sen said.

As part of the deal, Unocal can receive additional payments from Tosco of up to $250 million over seven years if California marketing margins improve, though analysts noted that this is a very large unknown.
"I wonder if they (Unocal) might not have done better from an aggregate shareholder standpoint from a tax-free spin-off," said Mark Gilman, an analyst at UBS Securities.

"The most interesting question for Unocal is what the market is going to say about it from a valuation point of view," Gilman added. Unocal's shares were up from Friday's close of $39-1/2 at $40-1/2, though Gilman said he was sticking with his valuation for the company of just $31 to $32 a share.
